story.hook: The Store Said My Receipt Wasn't Enough
story.script: I bought a new coffee machine as a birthday gift for my mother, and before I even wrapped it, I noticed the box had already been opened. The security tape had been cut and replaced with a strip of clear tape that looked like someone had done it in a hurry. I opened the box to check the machine and found water stains inside the tank, coffee grounds near the filter, and a handwritten service sticker underneath. It was obviously not new. I went back to the store the next afternoon with the machine, the box, and the original receipt. The employee at the returns counter looked at everything and told me they could not refund it because the machine had been used. I said that was exactly the problem. I had paid for a new machine and they had sold me one that somebody else had already used. She called over a supervisor, who repeated the same answer and pointed to their policy saying used appliances were not returnable. I asked him to look at the purchase time on my receipt and then at the service sticker under the machine. The sticker had a date from almost two months before I bought it. He barely looked at it. He said there was no way to prove I had not used the machine myself and that customers sometimes tried to return products after changing their minds. Then he offered me store credit for half the purchase price as a courtesy. That annoyed me more than a simple refusal would have, because now they were acting like I was asking for a favor. I asked if they could check the serial number. The supervisor said that would not change anything. So I took a photo of the service sticker, the serial number, the opened security seal, and my receipt while standing at the counter. Then I called the manufacturer's customer service number printed on the box. I explained that I had bought the machine as new but found a service sticker dated before my purchase. The representative asked for the serial number and went quiet for a moment. Then she told me something interesting. That exact machine had already been registered for warranty by another customer three months earlier. It had later been returned to the same retailer because of a leaking water pump. The manufacturer had a service record showing the repair date, the retailer location, and the serial number. I put the call on speaker and asked her to repeat that. The supervisor suddenly stopped talking. The representative emailed me the service confirmation while I was still standing there. It showed the machine had been repaired and returned to the retailer weeks before they sold it to me as new. I showed the email to the supervisor. He disappeared into the back office and came out with the store manager. The manager read the email, looked at the sticker, and immediately approved a full refund. Then she refunded the extended warranty I had bought with it and gave me a replacement machine from a sealed shipment at no charge. Before I left, she also asked for the name of the employee who had stocked the returned unit because repaired products were supposed to be marked and sold separately. The supervisor who had accused me of using it stood there silently while she processed everything. I came in asking for my money back on one used coffee machine. I left with the full refund, the warranty refunded too, and a brand-new replacement, all because the little service sticker they ignored had a date on it.

youtube.title: They Refused My Refund — Then the Serial Number Exposed Everything #Shorts
youtube.description: The store said I had used it. One tiny service sticker proved something very different.
